papers.title: TSEDTA: A Transformer-based neural network with SMILES Transformer and ESM2 embeddings for drug-target binding affinity prediction
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Drug-target binding affinity (DTA) prediction plays a vital role in drug repositioning. The emergence of large language models (LLMs) has introduced new perspectives for predicting DTA. Herein, we present TSEDTA, a Transformer-based neural network with SMILES Transformer and ESM2 embeddings for predicting DTA. It leverages pre-trained LLMs (SMILES Transformer and ESM2) to extract deep evolutionary representations from drug SMILES and protein sequences. The representations are directly fused with raw sequence embeddings and processed via dual Transformer encoders to capture complex local and global dependencies. Results The experiments demonstrate that TSEDTA outperforms ten advanced models on the Davis and KIBA datasets, and seven on the BindingDB dataset. Ablation studies show that incorporating LLM embeddings significantly improves the performance of TSEDTA. Furthermore, a practical case study demonstrates its real-world applicability. Ultimately, TSEDTA provides a highly accurate, robust tool for DTA prediction, offering new insights into the application of LLMs for DTA tasks. papers.title: Protein Language Model Embeddings Improve HIV Drug Resistance Prediction: A Comprehensive Benchmark with Attention-Based Interpretability
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Accurate prediction of HIV drug resistance from viral sequences is critical for optimising antiretroviral therapy. Traditional machine-learning approaches using binary mutation encoding achieve strong accuracy but may fail to capture epistatic interactions and structural features relevant to resistance mechanisms. Protein language models (PLMs) offer learned representations encoding evolutionary and structural information, but have not been systematically benchmarked for HIV resistance prediction across the modern antiretroviral drug set. Results We evaluated ESM-2 (650 M parameters) with attention-weighted pooling for predicting resistance to 18 drugs across three classes (protease inhibitors, NRTIs, NNRTIs) on the Stanford HIVDB dataset (n=6,308 sequences). Attention-weighted ESM-2 embeddings significantly outperformed XGBoost baselines with binary mutation encoding (mean AUC 0.968 vs 0.955, P=0.0017), with gains across 15 of 18 drugs and the largest improvements for drugs with complex resistance patterns. Attention weights showed 2.48-fold enrichment at known drug-resistance-mutation positions (P<0.05 for 63% of drugs; NRTIs strongest at 4.20-fold). External validation on a 20% holdout showed minimal degradation (AUC 0.934). Benchmarking against ESM C 600M and ESM-1v confirmed performance is robust to PLM choice (mean AUC 0.942–0.946 across backbones). Performance was maintained across HIV-1 subtypes (B 0.924; B-divergent 0.900; non-B 0.884) and a temporal holdout (AUC 0.930). Availability and Implementation Source code is available at https://github.com/hayden-farquhar/HIV-ESM-2 under an MIT licence and archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19466629 . Stanford HIVDB genotype-phenotype data are publicly available at https://hivdb.stanford.edu/

摘要：动机  
从病毒序列中准确预测HIV的耐药性对于优化抗逆转录病毒治疗至关重要。
llm_highlights_zh: 传统的基于二进制突变编码的机器学习方法虽然能够获得较高的准确率，但可能无法捕捉到与抗性机制相关的上位性相互作用及结构特征。
蛋白质语言模型能够生成蕴含进化与结构信息的表示形式，但目前尚未针对现代抗逆转录病毒药物库中的各种药物，对这些模型在预测HIV耐药性方面的性能进行系统的评估与测试。
我们在斯坦福HIVDB数据集（包含6,308条序列）上，评估了采用注意力加权池化技术的ESM-2模型（该模型包含650个参数），测试其预测病毒对三类药物（蛋白酶抑制剂、NRTIs类药物、NNRTIs类药物）的耐药性的能力。
papers.llm_rss_summary_zh:
**摘要**  
准确预测病毒序列中的HIV耐药性对于优化抗逆转录病毒治疗至关重要。传统的基于二进制突变编码的机器学习方法虽然能够取得较高的预测精度，但可能无法捕捉到与耐药机制相关的表观遗传相互作用及结构特征。蛋白质语言模型则能够编码这些进化与结构信息，但目前尚未针对现代抗逆转录病毒药物体系进行系统的性能评估。  

**研究结果**  
我们在Stanford HIVDB数据集（包含6,308条序列）上，使用具有注意力加权机制的ESM-2模型（含有6.5亿个参数）来预测病毒对18种不同类别抗逆转录病毒药物的耐药性。结果表明，与采用二进制突变编码的XGBoost基线方法相比，ESM-2模型的平均AUC值显著更高（0.968 vs 0.955，P=0.0017）；在18种药物中，有15种的预测效果得到了提升，尤其是对于那些耐药机制较为复杂的药物，其性能提升更为明显。实验数据显示，在已知与药物耐药性相关的突变位点上，ESM-2模型对这些突变的编码能力增强了2.48倍（其中63%的药物在这一指标上的提升幅度超过2.48倍，NRTI类药物的提升幅度最高，达到了4.20倍）。通过20%的数据进行外部验证时，该模型的预测性能仅略有下降（AUC值为0.934）。与ESM C 600M及ESM-1v模型相比，该模型的性能具有较好的稳定性，不同类型的蛋白质语言模型对其预测效果的影响不大（平均AUC值在0.942至0.946之间）。此外，该模型在HIV-1的不同亚型中均表现良好（B亚型的AUC值为0.924；B亚型衍生株的AUC值为0.900；非B亚型的AUC值为0.884），并且在时间跨度较大的数据集中也能保持稳定的预测能力（AUC值为0.930）。  

**代码与资源**  
该模型的源代码可访问https://github.com/hayden-farquhar/HIV-ESM-2，采用MIT许可证进行发布；相关研究数据已存档于https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19466629。Stanford HIVDB的基因型-表型数据也可公开获取，网址为https://hivdb.stanford.edu/。

papers.title: IDAP: An integrated literature- and knowledge-graph-driven evidence prioritization pipeline for precision oncology
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Advances in tumor sequencing enable routine detection of dozens to hundreds of somatic alterations per patient, yet only a minority can be linked to established therapeutic evidence. Curated resources such as OncoKB provide high-quality variant-drug annotations but remain limited in coverage, particularly for rare or low-frequency variants. This coverage gap motivates computational frameworks that can integrate curated, literature-derived, graph-based, and clinical-trial evidence to prioritize therapeutic hypotheses for expert review. Results We developed the Integrated Drug Annotation Pipeline (IDAP), a modular framework that combines four complementary evidence streams: curated variant-drug associations from OncoKB, literature-derived gene-drug mention counts from PubMed abstracts, graph-based drug prioritization using a TxGNN-derived biomedical knowledge graph, and cancer-specific clinical-trial evidence from ClinicalTrials.gov. Given a cancer type and a MAF file, IDAP generates patient-level reports summarizing detected variants, ranked therapeutic hypotheses, supporting evidence layers, and relevant clinical trials. Evaluated across five cancer types (n = 50 samples), IDAP expanded evidence-linked therapeutic hypotheses beyond curated databases alone. Among patients without OncoKB recommendations (26/50), IDAP identified a median of 87 candidate drugs (range: 2–473). To reduce cross-source scale imbalance, the final ranking used within-sample percentile normalization with fixed bonuses for curated evidence, multi-source support, and trial linkage. Under this revised ranking, 24/50 top-ranked candidates were supported by at least two evidence sources and 44/50 had associated ClinicalTrials metadata. In an exploratory external CIViC comparison, IDAP recovered at least one matched CIViC-supported therapy in 28/41 eligible samples, with 13/41 appearing within the top 10 candidates. These outputs are intended to support evidence triage and translational interpretation rather than direct treatment recommendation. Availability and implementation IDAP is freely available at https://github.com/joonan-lab/IDAP-pipeline , with full documentation at https://joonan-lab.github.io/IDAP-pipeline . An archived snapshot of the code used in this study is deposited on Zenodo (DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19301367 )

papers.llm_rss_summary_zh:
**摘要**  
肿瘤测序技术的进步使得能够为每位患者检测出数十至数百种体细胞变异，但其中仅有少数变异与现有的治疗手段存在关联。像OncoKB这样的专业资源虽然提供了高质量的变异-药物关联信息，但其覆盖范围仍然有限，尤其是对于那些罕见或低频出现的变异而言。这种数据覆盖不足的问题促使人们开发出能够整合各类整理过的信息、文献资料、基于图谱的分析方法以及临床试验数据的计算框架，以便为专家评估提供更有依据的治疗建议。  

**研究结果**  
我们开发了“集成药物注释管道”（IDAP），这一模块化框架结合了四种互补的证据来源：OncoKB提供的变异-药物关联信息、从PubMed摘要中提取的基因-药物关联数据、基于TxGNN构建的生物医学知识图谱所进行的药物优先级排序，以及ClinicalTrials.gov网站上的癌症相关临床试验数据。给定某种癌症类型及相应的MAF文件后，IDAP能够生成包含患者检测结果、排名靠前的治疗建议、支持这些建议的证据来源以及相关临床试验信息的报告。  

在五种不同类型的癌症样本中进行的测试显示，IDAP提供的证据关联治疗建议远远超出了传统数据库所能覆盖的范围。对于那些没有OncoKB推荐的药物而言，IDAP平均能为26名患者识别出87种候选药物（范围为2至473种）。为了解决数据来源间的不平衡问题，最终的排序结果采用了样本内百分位数标准化方法，并对来自不同来源的证据给予了不同的权重：整理过的数据库信息、多源证据的支持情况以及临床试验数据的关联程度都被纳入了排名考量。在这种调整后的排序体系中，前24名候选药物中均有至少两种证据来源为其提供支持，而前44种候选药物都包含了相关的ClinicalTrials元数据。  

在进一步的外部验证中，IDAP在41个符合条件的样本中成功找到了至少一种与CIViC数据库中的信息相匹配的治疗方案，其中13种候选药物甚至位列排名前十的位置。这些研究成果旨在为临床决策提供参考，而非直接用于制定治疗建议。  

**可获取性与实施方式**  
IDAP工具可免费在https://github.com/joonan-lab/IDAP-pipeline下载，其完整使用文档则位于https://joonan-lab.github.io/IDAP-pipeline。本研究所使用的代码版本也已存档在Zenodo平台上，可供查阅（DOI：https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19301367）。

papers.primary_summary_raw: Advances in tumor sequencing enable routine detection of dozens to hundreds of somatic alterations per patient, yet only a minority can be linked to established therapeutic evidence. Curated resources such as OncoKB provide high-quality variant-drug annotations but remain limited in coverage, particularly for rare or low-frequency variants. This coverage gap motivates computational frameworks that can integrate curated, literature-derived, graph-based, and clinical-trial evidence to prioritize therapeutic hypotheses for expert review. Results We developed the Integrated Drug Annotation Pipeline (IDAP), a modular framework that combines four complementary evidence streams: curated variant-drug associations from OncoKB, literature-derived gene-drug mention counts from PubMed abstracts, graph-based drug prioritization using a TxGNN-derived biomedical knowledge graph, and cancer-specific clinical-trial evidence from ClinicalTrials.gov. Given a cancer type and a MAF file, IDAP generates patient-level reports summarizing detected variants, ranked therapeutic hypotheses, supporting evidence layers, and relevant clinical trials. Evaluated across five cancer types (n = 50 samples), IDAP expanded evidence-linked therapeutic hypotheses beyond curated databases alone. Among patients without OncoKB recommendations (26/50), IDAP identified a median of 87 candidate drugs (range: 2–473). To reduce cross-source scale imbalance, the final ranking used within-sample percentile normalization with fixed bonuses for curated evidence, multi-source support, and trial linkage. Under this revised ranking, 24/50 top-ranked candidates were supported by at least two evidence sources and 44/50 had associated ClinicalTrials metadata. In an exploratory external CIViC comparison, IDAP recovered at least one matched CIViC-supported therapy in 28/41 eligible samples, with 13/41 appearing within the top 10 candidates. These outputs are intended to support evidence triage and translational interpretation rather than direct treatment recommendation.

all_papers.title: TSEDTA: A Transformer-based neural network with SMILES Transformer and ESM2 embeddings for drug-target binding affinity prediction
all_papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Drug-target binding affinity (DTA) prediction plays a vital role in drug repositioning. The emergence of large language models (LLMs) has introduced new perspectives for predicting DTA. Herein, we present TSEDTA, a Transformer-based neural network with SMILES Transformer and ESM2 embeddings for predicting DTA. It leverages pre-trained LLMs (SMILES Transformer and ESM2) to extract deep evolutionary representations from drug SMILES and protein sequences. The representations are directly fused with raw sequence embeddings and processed via dual Transformer encoders to capture complex local and global dependencies. Results The experiments demonstrate that TSEDTA outperforms ten advanced models on the Davis and KIBA datasets, and seven on the BindingDB dataset. Ablation studies show that incorporating LLM embeddings significantly improves the performance of TSEDTA. Furthermore, a practical case study demonstrates its real-world applicability. Ultimately, TSEDTA provides a highly accurate, robust tool for DTA prediction, offering new insights into the application of LLMs for DTA tasks. all_papers.title: Protein Language Model Embeddings Improve HIV Drug Resistance Prediction: A Comprehensive Benchmark with Attention-Based Interpretability
all_papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Accurate prediction of HIV drug resistance from viral sequences is critical for optimising antiretroviral therapy. Traditional machine-learning approaches using binary mutation encoding achieve strong accuracy but may fail to capture epistatic interactions and structural features relevant to resistance mechanisms. Protein language models (PLMs) offer learned representations encoding evolutionary and structural information, but have not been systematically benchmarked for HIV resistance prediction across the modern antiretroviral drug set. Results We evaluated ESM-2 (650 M parameters) with attention-weighted pooling for predicting resistance to 18 drugs across three classes (protease inhibitors, NRTIs, NNRTIs) on the Stanford HIVDB dataset (n=6,308 sequences). Attention-weighted ESM-2 embeddings significantly outperformed XGBoost baselines with binary mutation encoding (mean AUC 0.968 vs 0.955, P=0.0017), with gains across 15 of 18 drugs and the largest improvements for drugs with complex resistance patterns. Attention weights showed 2.48-fold enrichment at known drug-resistance-mutation positions (P<0.05 for 63% of drugs; NRTIs strongest at 4.20-fold). External validation on a 20% holdout showed minimal degradation (AUC 0.934). Benchmarking against ESM C 600M and ESM-1v confirmed performance is robust to PLM choice (mean AUC 0.942–0.946 across backbones). Performance was maintained across HIV-1 subtypes (B 0.924; B-divergent 0.900; non-B 0.884) and a temporal holdout (AUC 0.930). Availability and Implementation Source code is available at https://github.com/hayden-farquhar/HIV-ESM-2 under an MIT licence and archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19466629 . Stanford HIVDB genotype-phenotype data are publicly available at https://hivdb.stanford.edu/

准确预测病毒序列中的HIV耐药性对于优化抗逆转录病毒治疗至关重要。传统的基于二进制突变编码的机器学习方法虽然能够取得较高的预测精度，但可能无法捕捉到与耐药机制相关的表观遗传相互作用及结构特征。蛋白质语言模型则能够编码这些进化与结构信息，但目前尚未针对现代抗逆转录病毒药物体系进行系统的性能评估。  

**研究结果**  
我们在Stanford HIVDB数据集（包含6,308条序列）上，使用具有注意力加权机制的ESM-2模型（含有6.5亿个参数）来预测病毒对18种不同类别抗逆转录病毒药物的耐药性。结果表明，与采用二进制突变编码的XGBoost基线方法相比，ESM-2模型的平均AUC值显著更高（0.968 vs 0.955，P=0.0017）；在18种药物中，有15种的预测效果得到了提升，尤其是对于那些耐药机制较为复杂的药物，其性能提升更为明显。实验数据显示，在已知与药物耐药性相关的突变位点上，ESM-2模型对这些突变的编码能力增强了2.48倍（其中63%的药物在这一指标上的提升幅度超过2.48倍，NRTI类药物的提升幅度最高，达到了4.20倍）。通过20%的数据进行外部验证时，该模型的预测性能仅略有下降（AUC值为0.934）。与ESM C 600M及ESM-1v模型相比，该模型的性能具有较好的稳定性，不同类型的蛋白质语言模型对其预测效果的影响不大（平均AUC值在0.942至0.946之间）。此外，该模型在HIV-1的不同亚型中均表现良好（B亚型的AUC值为0.924；B亚型衍生株的AUC值为0.900；非B亚型的AUC值为0.884），并且在时间跨度较大的数据集中也能保持稳定的预测能力（AUC值为0.930）。  

**代码与资源**  
该模型的源代码可访问https://github.com/hayden-farquhar/HIV-ESM-2，采用MIT许可证进行发布；相关研究数据已存档于https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19466629。Stanford HIVDB的基因型-表型数据也可公开获取，网址为https://hivdb.stanford.edu/。

all_papers.primary_summary_raw: Accurate prediction of HIV drug resistance from viral sequences is critical for optimising antiretroviral therapy. Traditional machine-learning approaches using binary mutation encoding achieve strong accuracy but may fail to capture epistatic interactions and structural features relevant to resistance mechanisms. Protein language models (PLMs) offer learned representations encoding evolutionary and structural information, but have not been systematically benchmarked for HIV resistance prediction across the modern antiretroviral drug set. Results We evaluated ESM-2 (650 M parameters) with attention-weighted pooling for predicting resistance to 18 drugs across three classes (protease inhibitors, NRTIs, NNRTIs) on the Stanford HIVDB dataset (n=6,308 sequences). Attention-weighted ESM-2 embeddings significantly outperformed XGBoost baselines with binary mutation encoding (mean AUC 0.968 vs 0.955, P=0.0017), with gains across 15 of 18 drugs and the largest improvements for drugs with complex resistance patterns. Attention weights showed 2.48-fold enrichment at known drug-resistance-mutation positions (P<0.05 for 63% of drugs; NRTIs strongest at 4.20-fold). External validation on a 20% holdout showed minimal degradation (AUC 0.934). Benchmarking against ESM C 600M and ESM-1v confirmed performance is robust to PLM choice (mean AUC 0.942–0.946 across backbones). Performance was maintained across HIV-1 subtypes (B 0.924; B-divergent 0.900; non-B 0.884) and a temporal holdout (AUC 0.930).

all_papers.title: IDAP: An integrated literature- and knowledge-graph-driven evidence prioritization pipeline for precision oncology
all_papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Advances in tumor sequencing enable routine detection of dozens to hundreds of somatic alterations per patient, yet only a minority can be linked to established therapeutic evidence. Curated resources such as OncoKB provide high-quality variant-drug annotations but remain limited in coverage, particularly for rare or low-frequency variants. This coverage gap motivates computational frameworks that can integrate curated, literature-derived, graph-based, and clinical-trial evidence to prioritize therapeutic hypotheses for expert review. Results We developed the Integrated Drug Annotation Pipeline (IDAP), a modular framework that combines four complementary evidence streams: curated variant-drug associations from OncoKB, literature-derived gene-drug mention counts from PubMed abstracts, graph-based drug prioritization using a TxGNN-derived biomedical knowledge graph, and cancer-specific clinical-trial evidence from ClinicalTrials.gov. Given a cancer type and a MAF file, IDAP generates patient-level reports summarizing detected variants, ranked therapeutic hypotheses, supporting evidence layers, and relevant clinical trials. Evaluated across five cancer types (n = 50 samples), IDAP expanded evidence-linked therapeutic hypotheses beyond curated databases alone. Among patients without OncoKB recommendations (26/50), IDAP identified a median of 87 candidate drugs (range: 2–473). To reduce cross-source scale imbalance, the final ranking used within-sample percentile normalization with fixed bonuses for curated evidence, multi-source support, and trial linkage. Under this revised ranking, 24/50 top-ranked candidates were supported by at least two evidence sources and 44/50 had associated ClinicalTrials metadata. In an exploratory external CIViC comparison, IDAP recovered at least one matched CIViC-supported therapy in 28/41 eligible samples, with 13/41 appearing within the top 10 candidates. These outputs are intended to support evidence triage and translational interpretation rather than direct treatment recommendation. Availability and implementation IDAP is freely available at https://github.com/joonan-lab/IDAP-pipeline , with full documentation at https://joonan-lab.github.io/IDAP-pipeline . An archived snapshot of the code used in this study is deposited on Zenodo (DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19301367 )

all_papers.llm_rss_summary_zh:
**摘要**  
肿瘤测序技术的进步使得能够为每位患者检测出数十至数百种体细胞变异，但其中仅有少数变异与现有的治疗手段存在关联。像OncoKB这样的专业资源虽然提供了高质量的变异-药物关联信息，但其覆盖范围仍然有限，尤其是对于那些罕见或低频出现的变异而言。这种数据覆盖不足的问题促使人们开发出能够整合各类整理过的信息、文献资料、基于图谱的分析方法以及临床试验数据的计算框架，以便为专家评估提供更有依据的治疗建议。  

**研究结果**  
我们开发了“集成药物注释管道”（IDAP），这一模块化框架结合了四种互补的证据来源：OncoKB提供的变异-药物关联信息、从PubMed摘要中提取的基因-药物关联数据、基于TxGNN构建的生物医学知识图谱所进行的药物优先级排序，以及ClinicalTrials.gov网站上的癌症相关临床试验数据。给定某种癌症类型及相应的MAF文件后，IDAP能够生成包含患者检测结果、排名靠前的治疗建议、支持这些建议的证据来源以及相关临床试验信息的报告。  

在五种不同类型的癌症样本中进行的测试显示，IDAP提供的证据关联治疗建议远远超出了传统数据库所能覆盖的范围。对于那些没有OncoKB推荐的药物而言，IDAP平均能为26名患者识别出87种候选药物（范围为2至473种）。为了解决数据来源间的不平衡问题，最终的排序结果采用了样本内百分位数标准化方法，并对来自不同来源的证据给予了不同的权重：整理过的数据库信息、多源证据的支持情况以及临床试验数据的关联程度都被纳入了排名考量。在这种调整后的排序体系中，前24名候选药物中均有至少两种证据来源为其提供支持，而前44种候选药物都包含了相关的ClinicalTrials元数据。  

在进一步的外部验证中，IDAP在41个符合条件的样本中成功找到了至少一种与CIViC数据库中的信息相匹配的治疗方案，其中13种候选药物甚至位列排名前十的位置。这些研究成果旨在为临床决策提供参考，而非直接用于制定治疗建议。  

**可获取性与实施方式**  
IDAP工具可免费在https://github.com/joonan-lab/IDAP-pipeline下载，其完整使用文档则位于https://joonan-lab.github.io/IDAP-pipeline。本研究所使用的代码版本也已存档在Zenodo平台上，可供查阅（DOI：https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19301367）。

IDAP工具可免费在https://github.com/joonan-lab/IDAP-pipeline下载，其完整使用文档则位于https://joonan-lab.github.io/IDAP-pipeline。本研究所使用的代码版本也已存档在Zenodo平台上，可供查阅（DOI：https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19301367）。
